document_0002.source_limits: King & Saraf re-test the central claim of Ioannou & Serafeim (2015), I&S: that over 1993-2007 sell-side analysts' recommendations became less pessimistic for firms with high CSR (KLD) strengths. They state that they 'analyze the same data, use the same statistical models, and recreate the main tables', rebuilding the original sample from the same databases (Compustat, CRSP, I/B/E/S, KLD; N=16,088 vs 16,064 originally). I therefore code a reproduction (re-analysis of the original study's data) rather than a new-sample replication. Part of the extension adds new years through 2016; that new-data portion is not used for the robustness axis. Single original paper, one target; the replication paper reports no numbered studies. Axis 1 (computation): the re-run produced numbers, but they did not recover the original pattern. The authors write 'Unlike I&S', report no substantive or significant change in the CSR coefficient over time, and say Tables 3-4 provide no support for the principal hypothesis. They also report coefficient differences for market value and long-term forecast error, and the replicated auxiliary/robustness analyses differ from I&S. This is coded 'computational issues'. Descriptive statistics broadly conform. The divergence may partly reflect reconstruction choices, such as lag structure and the forecast-error formula; the original authors did not respond. Axis 2 (robustness): alternative specifications of the original 1993-2007 frame removed the claimed temporal shift: CSR x linear time, CSR x year dummies, and analyst-level models with analyst fixed effects. The authors conclude that the finding 'is not as robust as previously suggested'. This is coded 'robustness challenges'. A qualifier is that the analyst-level models show a positive linear trend for CSR concerns, significant only in the extended (new-data) sample, and a lone significant 1996 strengths estimate. Source limits: the supplied text is pdftotext output. Tables 3, 4 and 6 and Figures 1-3 appear only as captions, so the reproduced coefficients for the main tables cannot be inspected. I rely on the authors' prose. No DOI for I&S is printed in the reference list. Ioannou & Serafeim's reference entry is copied with line-wrap hyphenation removed in the title field.

document_0003.source_limits: Wismans et al. (2020), a 'Replication Note', re-test in a new sample a finding from Yu, Wiklund & Pérez-Luño (2018). The new sample comprises 802 French SME owners from three Amarok survey waves. Yu et al., using Spanish and mainly US samples, found that firm-level EO is positively related to the hyperactivity/impulsivity dimension of ADHD and unrelated to the attention-deficit dimension. This is a replication (new data, individual-level EO, different controls) with one target. The 2018 Academy of Management Proceedings version is named because the authors cite it throughout and state that they based the replication on it rather than the forthcoming 2020 ETP version. Its DOI is printed in the reference list. Outcome: there is no single overall verdict, but the discussion compares both of Yu et al.'s dimension-level results. Hyperactivity is positively associated with total EO ('Similar to Yu et al.'; 'we are able to replicate the positive relationship found by Yu et al. (2018) between hyperactivity and EO'). Attention-deficit is not associated with total EO, which agrees with Yu et al.'s null. The authors call their results 'mostly in line' with Yu et al., and no result is marked as contrasting with the original, so this is coded successful. The null total-ADHD-EO link and the EO subdimension results are extensions: the paper states that no prior study examined overall ADHD and EO and that Yu et al. did not split EO. They therefore do not count against the replication verdict. Qualifiers: the word 'mostly'; differing controls; low alpha for hyperactivity (.51); individual- rather than firm-level EO. Thurik et al. (2016, retracted) is not coded as a target. The paper says it 'redo[es] the analysis of Thurik et al. (2016)' on an overlapping sample, but with the stated aim of replicating Yu et al. It never states or compares against a Thurik et al. finding. Source limits: text is a cached parse of the published PDF. Tables 2 and 3 are rotated and extracted one character per line; their values were read only as scrambled characters, and the coding relies on the prose results and discussion. A machine-parsed reference list is appended after the article references.
